summary: Reconcile signed fleet membership into Fabric runtime peers and report local policy status (#2842)

replay.detail: No graph replay or admission-format change. Runtime Fabric policy is derived from the existing signed fleet membership view.

schema.detail: No database migration. The worker records local reconciliation state in fleet/fabric-reconcile.json; fleet and replication status expose state, message and policy_revision.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rules or coordinated member upgrade. Fleet membership remains authoritative for the st/fleet/<fleet-id> runtime policy owner.

compatibility.detail: Fabric-enabled workers manage owner-scoped runtime peers and protocol grants without rewriting static configuration. Existing static peers and independently owned grants remain independent. Online leave requires an upgraded confirming member for the authenticated leave-receipt endpoint; unsupported peers cannot falsely complete leave. Status reports pending or error instead of assuming runtime policy success.

downtime.detail: No coordinated fleet downtime is required. Runtime policy management requires a Fabric daemon started with --runtime-peers; status reports runtime_peers_disabled when that capability is unavailable. Static peers still work.

manual.detail: For runtime membership management, restart Fabric with --runtime-peers when fleet or replication status reports runtime_peers_disabled. No static peer file edits or extra daemon are required.

recovery.detail: Membership refresh reconciles the owner's desired runtime policy, including ended members. Before replaying an uncertain transaction, st revalidates every operation against the latest signed membership and exact grants; obsolete additions are queried but never resubmitted. Leave retains only its replication carrier until authenticated completion, withdrawing PTY and gateway grants immediately. Fleet and replication status retain failures and distinguish leaving from applied. Other owners or static policy may retain rights after this owner's records are withdrawn.
